final_message:
All five implementations are complete and verified.

## Algorithm (shared across all five languages)

Single pass over the input file (path = first argv), read entirely into memory:
1. Split on `\n`; each line is validated char-by-char/byte-by-byte against the full SPEC grammar — timestamp positions/digits/separators, `[a-z]+-\d+` host, method (GET/PUT/POST/DELETE/PATCH by literal byte compare), path `/[A-Za-z0-9_/-]*` + optional `?query`, `\d{3}` status, `\d+B` size, `\d+.\dms` latency, `"..."` UA, and end-of-line. Anything deviating is malformed.
2. Well-formed lines: increment status class `Cxx`; compute path template by splitting on `/`, replacing each non-empty all-digit segment with `{id}`, rejoining with `/` (trailing/internal slashes preserved); accumulate latency in tenths of ms per template.
3. Report: `lines L`, `malformed M`, `status Cxx N` per occurring class ascending, then up to 10 `path TEMPLATE COUNT P50 P95 MAX` sorted by count desc, then template byte order ascending. Percentile = nearest rank at 1-based position `ceil(p*n/100)`, computed with integer math `(p*n+99)/100 - 1`. Latency printed as `t/10.t%10` (one decimal). Output written as raw bytes with LF only, single `write` at the end. Single thread/process, only the input file is read, nothing precomputed or embedded.

## Per-language speed choices

- **C++20** (`cpp/main.cpp`): manual `const char*` parser, `unordered_map<string, Stats, SVHash, SVEq>` with FNV-1a hash and transparent `string_view` lookup (only unique templates allocated), per-template `vector<int>` with `reserve(16)`, `std::sort`, `_setmode(_fileno(stdout), _O_BINARY)` + `fwrite` for LF-exact output. Builds via `cpp\build.cmd` (`/O2 /GL /EHsc /std:c++20`).
- **Java 23** (`java/src/Main.java`): `Files.readString` US_ASCII, custom `TMap` open-addressing map (hash31) with interned String keys and `char[]` transparent lookup, growable `int[]` latencies, `System.out.write` of raw ASCII bytes. Builds via `java\build.cmd`, runs via `java/run.cmd`.
- **C# .NET 8** (`csharp/Program.cs`): manual `byte[]` parser with `stackalloc`-friendly `char[128]` template buffer, sealed `TMap` open addressing (FNV-1a), `Array.Sort` with count-desc then `CompareOrdinal`, `Console.OpenStandardOutput` raw bytes. Unchanged `.csproj` (Release, Optimize). Builds via `csharp\build.cmd`.
- **Go 1.27** (`go/main.go`): byte-slice manual parser over `os.ReadFile`, custom open-addressing `TMap` (FNV-1a) with interned string keys and byte-slice transparent comparison, `sort.Ints` per template, single `os.Stdout.Write`. Std lib only, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`. Builds via `go\build.cmd`.
- **Node 22** (`js/main.js`): `Buffer` byte parser (all comparisons on byte values), `Map<string, Stats>` keyed by the interned template string, `Array.sort` with numeric compare, `process.stdout.write(out.join('\n') + '\n')`. Built-in modules only.

## Verification results

All five versions produce byte-identical output for every sample:

| Version | s1.in | s2.in | s3.in | t1.in | big.in (300k lines, vs ref.py) |
|---------|-------|-------|-------|-------|--------------------------------|
| C++     | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS |
| Java    | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS |
| C#      | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS |
| Go      | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS |
| JS      | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS  | PASS |

Big.in was a generated 300k-line, 27 MB mixed valid/malformed input compared against the Python reference (`ref.py`) byte-for-byte; all five matched. `ref.py` was used only for testing, as scoped. Temporary test artifacts were removed; the tree contains the five implementations plus the pre-existing samples and expected outputs.

No commits were made (not a git repository).

request.prompt:
You are writing five versions of the same program, in C++, Java, C#, Go and JavaScript, for a comparison of
how fast and how memory-hungry each version is.

The task is described in SPEC.md in this folder. The folder samples/ holds example inputs (`*.in`), each with
the exact expected output (`*.out`).

Each language has its own folder with a starting file and a `build.cmd`. The benchmark builds every program with
these same build scripts and flags, whatever you change in them. Write these programs:

1. `cpp/main.cpp` (more `.cpp` and header files in `cpp/` are fine): C++20, built by `cpp\build.cmd` with
   Microsoft Visual C++ 19.40 (Visual Studio 2022) and `/O2 /GL /EHsc /std:c++20`. Standard library only, plus
   nlohmann/json 3.12 (`#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>`, already in `cpp/include/`). Run as
   `cpp\solution.exe INPUT_PATH`.
2. `java/src/Main.java` (more `.java` files in `java/src/` are fine): Java 23, built by `java\build.cmd` with
   `javac`. Java SE only, plus Jackson 2.22 (core, databind and annotations, already in `java/lib/`). Run as
   `java\run.cmd INPUT_PATH`, which runs `java -cp "out;lib\*" Main` with the default JVM settings.
3. `csharp/Program.cs` (more `.cs` files in `csharp/` are fine): C# 12 on .NET 8, built in Release by
   `csharp\build.cmd`. Base class library only. You may change properties in `csharp/solution.csproj`, but do not
   add package references. Run as `csharp\out\solution.exe INPUT_PATH`.
4. `go/main.go` (more `.go` files in `go/` are fine): Go 1.27, built by `go\build.cmd`. Standard library only.
   Run as `go\solution.exe INPUT_PATH`.
5. `js/main.js`: JavaScript on Node.js 22, with no build step. Built-in Node modules only; no npm packages. Run as
   `node js\main.js INPUT_PATH`.

Each program reads the input file whose path is its first argument (SPEC.md says if a task takes more
arguments) and writes the answer to standard output exactly as SPEC.md describes.

Your goals, in order:

1. Every version must print the correct output for any valid input as SPEC.md defines it, not only for the
   samples.
2. Make each version as fast as you can. Write each one the way a skilled developer in that language would
   write fast code, using that language's own strengths.

Use a single thread and a single process unless SPEC.md says otherwise. Do not precompute or embed answers,
start other programs, or read any file other than the input. Python 3.13 (`C:\Python313\python.exe`) is
available if you want it for testing, but not as part of any program.

The programs will be run on Windows 11 on a 16-core laptop, on larger inputs of the same kind; SPEC.md gives
the benchmark size. Build and test all five versions against every sample before you finish. Work only inside
this folder, and take at most about 60 minutes. Other programs run on this machine at the same time: never stop
a process you did not start yourself, so do not kill processes by name (for example `taskkill /IM java.exe` or
`Stop-Process -Name node`); stop only your own processes, by process ID.

When you are done, reply with a short summary: the algorithm, the main choices you made for speed in each
version, and which samples each version passes.
